I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because in Quzhou County that is the safest way for me to earn from one field twice in one year. I will plant winter wheat on all my land first, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same land. I will not spread myself across many crops, because that adds market risk, labor trouble, and management mistakes. I want crops I know, crops with stable local buyers, and crops that fit our water and weather conditions.

For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most fertilizer on at sowing and then topdress nitrogen once when the crop is growing strongly. I will irrigate a few key times instead of watering too often, because water matters most at the main growth stages. I will manage weeds, rust, and aphids with limited pesticide sprays only when needed. I will use rotary tillage before wheat so the seedbed is even and I get a uniform stand.

After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize. I will use hybrid maize because I want stronger yield and a more even crop. I will keep the turnaround fast so I do not lose moisture or sow too late. I will use less tillage for maize, mainly to save time and hold moisture after wheat. I will fertilize with nitrogen as the main driver, with some phosphorus and potassium, and I will irrigate only when the crop really needs it. I will watch for armyworm, corn borer, and leaf disease, and I will keep pesticide use moderate. My whole plan is simple: two staple crops, steady inputs, careful timing, and no unnecessary risk.
